en: Udāna 4.7 Sāriputtasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now on that occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was sitting not far from the Blessed One,
having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and, being of few desires, contented, secluded, unentangled, energetic, and devoted to the higher mind.

The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, having folded his legs crosswise and set his body erect—one who was of few desires, contented, secluded, unattached, energetic, and devoted to the higher mind.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired exclamation:
“For one of lofty mind, who is heedful...”
For the sage who trains in the paths of silence,
for the one who is thusly composed,
peaceful, and ever mindful, sorrows do not come to pass.
